prompt: Without doing any arithmetic, how does $3 \times (245 + 17)$ compare with $245 + 17$?
hint: Both expressions contain the same piece, $245 + 17$. What is being done to that piece?

hints.text: Both expressions contain the same piece, $245 + 17$. What is being done to that piece?
The parentheses keep $245 + 17$ together as one chunk, and the $3$ multiplies that whole chunk.
Multiplying by $3$ makes it $3$ times as big.

explanation: Think of $245 + 17$ as one bundle, kept together by the parentheses.
The $3$ outside multiplies that entire bundle, so you have three copies of it.
That makes the first expression $3$ times as big as the second.
You never needed the actual total to see it — but if you check, $245 + 17 = 262$ and $3 \times 262 = 786$, which is indeed $3$ times $262$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Think in snack packs
steps: If one lunch bag holds $245$ crackers and $17$ grapes, that is one bundle.
Three bundles is $3 \times$ one bundle — three times as much, not three more items.
